subject: Recap: Performance SLOs, concurrency profile & proposed credits for FinWise pilot
messages:
From: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.com>
To: Tom Alvarez <tom.alvarez@finwise.com>
Cc: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 15 Sep 2026 16:05:00 -0700
Subject: Recap: Performance SLOs + concurrency profile (FinWise pilot)

Thanks again for the call earlier, Tom — good discussion. I wanted to capture the agreed items and a few clarifying questions so we can move to a pilot proposal.

Call summary (high level)
- Target p95 latency: 120–150 ms for 256-token responses; p99 target ~350 ms for burst traffic.
- Sustained throughput: ~100 req/s across the service with bursts to ~300 req/s for 3–5 minute windows.
- Concurrency model: you expect ~200 parallel user-facing requests at peak, with many short-lived streams (avg 8–12s).
- Streaming: progressive token streaming for UI; prefer WebSocket with keep-alive and ability to multiplex up to 4 logical streams per socket.
- Authentication: token-based, rotating keys via your internal gateway.

Open clarification items (please confirm):
1) Do you consider the 200 parallel figure to be "concurrent sessions" (long-lived) or concurrent active requests (short bursts)? We want to size connection pooling vs. session allocation correctly.
2) For streaming UX, are partial tokens displayed as they arrive (low-latency display) or do you buffer until sentence boundaries? This affects our batching strategy.

Proposed next steps from Redwood:
- We will draft a pilot configuration: dedicated pool with capacity for 220 concurrent connections, WebSocket multiplexing enabled, and automatic fallback to a compatible model variant when latency SLOs can't be met.
- Share a draft rate card and a small connection-profile CSV so you can validate client-side limits.
- Outline SLAs and a brief runbook for ramp (pilot -> production).

If that aligns, I’ll send the rate card + connection profile and a short MSA addendum for pilot credits. Would you be available for a 30-min follow-up on Friday to finalize numbers?

Thanks,
Irene
Irene Choi
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
irene.choi@redwood.com | +1 415-555-0123

--
Attachment stubs referenced: redwood-ratecard-v2.pdf (proposed pricing/rate bands), finwise-conn-profile.csv (sample connectivity matrix)

From: Tom Alvarez <tom.alvarez@finwise.com>
To: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.com>
Cc: Elena Garcia <elena.garcia@finwise.com>
Date: Wed, 16 Sep 2026 09:18:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Recap: Performance SLOs + concurrency profile (FinWise pilot)

Thanks, Irene — that captures the call well. A couple clarifications from our side:

- The 200 figure is concurrent active requests (short-lived, <15s) coming from our front-end pool. We expect ~8k daily active users; peak concurrency is tied to market open (3–5 minute spikes).
- For streaming, we stream tokens as they arrive — low-latency UI is critical, even if some early tokens may be partial.
- Authentication: we will use per-session short-lived tokens issued by our gateway; no mutual TLS required for the pilot.

One ask on commercial: because this is a production-feeling pilot (live users), we need a small SLA credit or usage credit if p99 exceeds 400 ms more than 2 times in a 30-day window during the pilot. Not a showstopper — just to reduce operational risk on our side.

Happy to do Friday; I can do 10:00–12:00 PT.

Tom
Tom Alvarez
Head of Engineering, FinWise Financial
tom.alvarez@finwise.com | +1 212-555-6789

From: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com>

Date: Thu, 17 Sep 2026 08:40:00 -0700
Subject: Internal: Draft offer for FinWise pilot (notes)

Internal notes before we send the formal packet to FinWise:

- Deal id: RDW-FW-2026-0915 (use in HubSpot).
- Proposed pilot configuration:
  * Dedicated pool (multi-tenant but logically isolated) with 220 concurrent connection allowance.
  * WebSocket keep-alive + multiplexing up to 4 streams per socket.
  * Autoscaling headroom for short bursts to 350 req/s for up to 5 minutes.
  * Model variant: rw-4f-lowlat (optimized kernels / quantized) as first pass; fallback to rw-4f-stable if errors/latency spike.
- Commercials:
  * Two-month pilot: 50k free tokens + $0.00 bill until ramp if SLOs met.
  * If p99 > 400 ms more than twice in 30 days, provide a one-time credit equal to 10% of pilot usage (cap $5k).
  * Post-pilot rate card per attachment; include notes on connection-based billing vs per-token to avoid surprises.
- Operational: prepare runbook for ramp days (market open), include sticky KV-cache config, prefix caching for prompt templates.

Questions for Irene / Marissa:
- Irene — confirm the thread we send to FinWise includes the attachments and a short note on how the multiplexing behaves under connection drops.
- Marissa — can you add an entry in HubSpot and schedule the Friday 10–10:30 PT follow-up?

-Aditya
Aditya Rao
Director, Solutions Sales, Redwood Inference

Tom — attaching the documents we discussed. Quick summary and asks below.

What’s attached:
- redwood-ratecard-v2.pdf — draft pricing for pilot and sample production bands.
- finwise-conn-profile.csv — sample connection/occupancy matrix calibrated to your "200 concurrent active requests" profile.

Key points in the packet:
- We propose a dedicated pilot pool sized for 220 concurrent connections, with multiplexing to reduce socket count and autoscale burst capacity to 350 req/s for short windows.
- For the pilot, we’ll include 50k token credits and the SLA credit clause (10% one-time credit, capped at $5k) if p99 > 400 ms twice in a 30-day rolling window.
- Authentication works with your per-session tokens; our gateway will accept rotating bearer tokens for the pilot.

DocuSign & scheduling:
- If this looks good, please sign the pilot addendum (DocuSign link below) and we’ll spin up the pool within 48 hours of signature.
  DocuSign: https://www.docusign.com/finwise-msa/abcdef-2026

Thanks — let me know if you want any changes to the rate bands or the connection profile before we send the DocuSign.

Best,
Irene
